solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit and a soft white cheese? No thanks!

indicators.note: refusing thanks means the short word for thanks is struck out of the cheese

blocks.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a fruit with a soft white cheese and declines politely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ricotta loses its final TA. 'Soft' looks like part of the cheese's description, but it is P on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Clumsy seller loses her charge

indicators.note: the seller's word gives up some of its letters, namely the pronoun that follows

blocks.note: a hawker sells goods in the street
taken as written; these letters are removed
a ward is someone in another's charge

explanation.surface: A careless saleswoman loses the child she was looking after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her charge' reads as one phrase, the child she minds, but splits: 'her' is the letters dropped from the seller, and 'charge' is a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and clumsy are synonyms for lacking grace or ease of movement.

clue.text: Game bird seen briefly up in the country

definitions.note: an adjective in the answer; 'in the country' means rural

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the bird's name loses its last letter
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: RU is rugby union, a game
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A game bird is glimpsed flying up somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' looks like one thing, a pheasant or grouse, but splits into a sport and a songbird. LARK is shortened to LAR, then turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things of the country as opposed to the town.

clue.text: Gossip about employer that's short

blocks.note: ca. (circa) means about
one who employs a tool is its user
i.e., short for id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A rumour about an employer is brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss, but here it is one who employs something. 'Short' tells you to write that's as its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is an informal chatty talk or essay, a kind of gossip borrowed from French.

clue.text: Rubbish written about female President

indicators.note: one word is written around another, enclosing it

blocks.note: tat is cheap rubbishy goods
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone writes nonsense about a woman president.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT goes around F.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th President of the United States.

clue.text: Dog and what its cruel owner is heard to do?

definitions.text: what its cruel owner is heard to do

blocks.note: first meaning: a slender racing dog breed

blocks.clueFragment: what its cruel owner is heard to do
blocks.note: second meaning: said aloud, the breed sounds like a cruel owner hitting the animal

explanation.surface: A dog breed and a grim joke about how a cruel owner treats it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: pronounced as two words, the breed's name is what a cruel owner does to the animal, hence 'is heard to do'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slender racing dog breed, like a small greyhound.

clue.text: Weird leek left out by gardener's friend?

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A strange leek gets left out by a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' does the shuffling, with L added in.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedkiller helps a gardener by destroying unwanted plants, so it is fairly called a friend, with a question mark for the whimsy.

clue.text: One artist has some old books — there's work to be done here!

definitions.text: there's work to be done here!

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament, a set of old books
Man Ray was a surrealist artist

explanation.surface: An artist owns old books and has a lot of work waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: I and RAY together hold NT. 'Artist' suggests RA, but the answer needs RAY, from Man Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is the office tray holding papers still awaiting attention, so work is waiting there.

clue.text: Criticise volume when I'm in show

indicators.note: the second phrase follows straight on, set inside the word just given
in places one item inside another

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
a tome is a large book or volume
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the sound level while appearing in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests loudness, but it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience participation.

clue.text: Fuss made about sailors and a very strong wind

indicators.note: made around something means built to enclose it

blocks.note: a to-do is a fuss
RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors complain about a fierce wind.
explanation.walkthrough: TO-DO surrounds RN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air, among the strongest winds known.

clue.text: Hoo-ha made by Royal pair with horrible fluff on rear of throne

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter
horrible means a mess, so these letters go into a new order

blocks.note: K for king and ER for the Queen make a royal pair
taken as written
the last letter of throne

explanation.surface: A royal couple cause a stir over something nasty on the back of the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: K (king) and ER (Elizabeth Regina) are two royal abbreviations. The shuffled fluff plus E follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoo-ha and kerfuffle are both informal words for a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Note heard by this singer

indicators.note: heard means going by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A singer hears a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music but is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, and 'this singer' points to the answer itself.

clue.text: Dozing snake seen around meadow

indicators.note: around places the first word on either side of the second

blocks.note: the asp is a venomous snake
lee is a variant spelling of lea, a meadow

explanation.surface: A snake lies sleeping in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The meadow is spelt here in a less common variant of lea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dozing is asleep, both describing a state of slumber.

clue.text: Vet left Omaha flying to reach a state further north

indicators.note: flying suggests something thrown about, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: to OK something is to vet and approve it
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet flies out of Omaha heading for a state to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' suggests an animal doctor but is a verb meaning approve. The definition is loose: Oklahoma lies north of Texas, though south of Omaha's Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is a US state, lying north of Texas in the southern central plains.

clue.text: Monk cleaving smoother poker

indicators.note: to cleave something is to split it, so one word wedges into the middle of another

blocks.note: a sander smooths wood
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A monk splits a smoothing tool with a fire iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker' suggests the card game, but is a metal rod for the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is an old iron utensil heated red-hot and used for browning food or lighting fires, like a poker.

clue.text: Some French guy, say, pinches very good bum

definitions.note: bum here is the slang adjective meaning worthless or rotten

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze something between, so the pair grip a short word

blocks.note: des is French for some
pi is slang for pious, very good
a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A Frenchman pinches a very attractive backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces together do the pinching. 'Guy' suggests a man but is a rope, and 'bum' is not the backside but the adjective meaning lousy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bum as an adjective means worthless or contemptible, as despicable does.

clue.text: Comedy hits get sign of approval

blocks.note: a slap is a hit
a tick mark shows something is approved

explanation.surface: Comedy hits win the critics' approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' looks like successes but is a plural noun for blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, named after a clown's prop.

clue.text: Steam iron captivates surrealist

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the end of steam and the start of iron

explanation.surface: A steam iron enchants a surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a Spanish painter associated with the surrealist movement.

clue.text: Miss cutting small portion in stone

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a dole is a small share or portion handed out
to miss something out is to omit it

explanation.surface: A young woman slices a tiny piece of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' suggests a young woman but is the verb meaning leave out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a mineral and the sedimentary rock made from it, a kind of stone.

clue.text: Idiot starts to play rough and act oddly

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters
oddly keeps the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on

blocks.note: the first letters of play and rough
the first and third letters of act

explanation.surface: An idiot begins to play rough and behave strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' covers only the first two words; 'and' then joins a second selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a fool or idiot.

clue.text: European court imprisons a weaselly type

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut something inside

blocks.note: a Pole is from Poland
CT is the abbreviation for court
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European court jails a shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaselly type' sounds like a sneaky person but is literal: the animal is a weasel relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a member of the weasel family, so literally a weaselly animal.

clue.text: Nasty dog's very old and fast

blocks.note: dog's read as dog is; a dog is a male animal, as against a bitch
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A nasty dog is very old and quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' suggests speed, but it is the religious fast, Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm to others, a stronger form of nasty.

clue.text: Paint member of agency staff joining Times

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An agency worker joins the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper but is an age or era.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk.

clue.text: Extremely likeable member of upper classes is fired

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of likeable
a toff is a British slang word for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A very pleasant aristocrat is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests dismissed from a job, but it means a gun or firework went off.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a gun or firework is to fire it, so let off can mean fired.

clue.text: Star takes young girl around entertainment centre

indicators.note: the young girl takes in the star, holding it inside
around puts the girl on both sides of the star

blocks.note: a lass is a girl, chiefly in Scotland and northern England
Vega is a bright star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a girl out to a nightspot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity but is a real star, the brightest in the constellation Lyra.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is famous for its casinos and shows, a centre of entertainment.

clue.text: Aussie playing it appears 11

blocks.note: first meaning: an Australian marsupial
second meaning: the animal in an idiom for pretending to be dead or sleeping, as at 11 across

explanation.surface: An Australian performer seems to be dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie' looks like a person, but names an animal from Australia. 11 across is ASLEEP, and to play possum is to feign sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Possums are tree-dwelling Australian marsupials, and 'playing possum' is an idiom for pretending to be asleep or dead.

clue.text: Fish under small rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places one piece below the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish lurks beneath a little rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a stone, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock something is to shake or sway it.

clue.text: Discern a good deal when schilling crashes

indicators.note: to crash in is to barge in at the front uninvited

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for schilling, the old Austrian currency
a pot, as in pots of money, is a good deal

explanation.surface: Someone notices a bargain as the Austrian currency collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' suggests a bargain, but it means a large amount, a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to discern or notice it.

clue.text: Endless clue about firm material? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
about signals one item going around another
this reverses the stated arrangement, so the outer and inner pieces swap roles

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A vague hint about some fabric from a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clipped clue goes around the firm; 'Just the opposite!' reverses that, so the firm goes around the clipped clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing twill cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: Cup tie with lad playing match

indicators.note: playing suggests letters moving around freely into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy plays in a football cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sports fixture, fitting the cup tie, but it means a copy or equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate is an exact copy, something that matches another; as a verb, to duplicate is to match.

clue.text: Mistakenly suppose Glastonbury feature is a copy for Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a copy is a fake, and Glastonbury Tor is a hill in Somerset, England; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a famous English landmark is a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glastonbury' suggests the music festival, but the feature is the Tor, the hill above the town.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone for another is to wrongly believe they are that person or thing.

clue.text: Article on "It girl"

blocks.note: the is the definite article
re means on or concerning
it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A magazine article about the latest 'It girl'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It girl' reads as one phrase but splits into It and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a girl's first name.
